- Top-center: green (N)
- All other cells: gray (g)

- Top-center: green (N)
- Middle-left: gray (g)
- Middle-right: gray (g)

- Middle-left: white (W) - changed from gray

Wait, let me think about this differently. The left grid has purple cells at diamond positions: top-center, middle-left, middle-right, bottom-center. So the mechanic seems to be: clicking a purple cell on the left grid toggles the corresponding cell on the right grid. But the top-center cell was already green, so it didn't change. The other three diamond cells turned white.
Wait, but the top-center cell on the right grid was already green before I clicked the left grid. So maybe the mechanic is: clicking a purple cell on the left grid sets the corresponding cell on the right grid to white (or toggles it).
Let me think about the goal. The left grid has purple cells at diamond positions. The right grid should match this pattern. Currently:
- Diamond cells: top-center=green, middle-left=white, middle-right=white, bottom-center=white
- Non-diamond cells: all gray
If the goal is to make the diamond cells white (matching the initial state), then I need to change the top-center cell from green to white. I can do this by clicking the top-center purple cell on the left grid again.
Let me try clicking the top-center purple cell on the left grid again to see if it toggles the top-center cell on the right grid from green to white.
